# Expertise

## Methods

Boateng's lab specializes in resolving conformationally heterogeneous
multi-subunit complexes by cryo-EM, using multi-state classification to
separate particle images into discrete conformational classes before
reconstruction rather than averaging across states [boateng2019hetero].
Once discrete states are separated, flexible fitting places atomic models
into the resulting lower-resolution density maps using a molecular-dynamics
flexible fitting protocol [boateng2022fit].

## Intellectual lineage

The multi-state classification approach extends single-particle cryo-EM
methods developed for rigid complexes, adapted to explicitly model
conformational heterogeneity rather than treating it as reconstruction
noise to be averaged out [boateng2019hetero].

## Recurring critiques

A recurring critique is that many published cryo-EM structures of flexible
complexes report a single consensus conformation that is, in effect, an
average over several real states, discarding exactly the information that
matters most for understanding how the complex functions
[boateng2019hetero, boateng2022fit].

## Career trajectory

Early work applied standard single-particle methods to rigid complexes;
the shift to multi-state classification [boateng2019hetero] followed once
it became clear that a subset of complexes of interest simply could not be
described by a single consensus structure. Flexible fitting work
[boateng2022fit] followed as a natural extension once discrete states were
separable.
